about

A student-run week of quantum computing.

Qiskit Fall Fest is a global season of student-led quantum events organised with IBM Quantum. In 2026 it comes to RV University, Bengaluru.

Each afternoon is a working session, not a lecture: you write circuits, run them on simulators and real IBM Quantum hardware, and leave with code that works. The week closes with a 24-hour hackathon where teams build something of their own on the ideas from the previous four days.

5days · 13–17 Oct

The IBM Quantum Challenge Hackathon starts the moment Friday's session ends and runs straight through to Saturday evening. Teams pick a prompt, build with Qiskit, and present working code — not slides.

  • Starts 16 Oct, 20:00 IST · ends 17 Oct, 20:00 IST

  • Mentors from the organising team on the floor all night
  • Open to everyone attending the workshop week

faq

Before you ask

Who can attend?

Any student, from any discipline. The sessions are built for people meeting quantum computing for the first time, and the later days go deep enough to stay interesting if you have seen it before.

Do I need to know quantum physics?

No. Comfort with basic Python and linear algebra helps, but day 1 starts from qubits and builds up from there.

What should I install beforehand?

Python 3 and Qiskit. A setup guide goes out to registered participants before day 1, and there is help at the start of the first session if anything breaks.

Do I have to attend all five days?

The days build on each other, so attending the full week is strongly recommended — especially if you plan to join the hackathon.

Will I get a certificate?

Certificate details are confirmed closer to the event and announced here.
